messages:
Ellen V: follow-up on model warmup: thinking about microshard affinity to reduce cross-host io. jotting down quick ideas before updating the RFC.
Marco P: affinity meaning we prefer serving requests likely to touch the same microshards on the same host?
Ellen V: yes. assign a hotset score per microshard based on recent hits; scheduler biases placement so hot microshards co-locate. reduces inter-host reads and network egress.
Zoe L: nice. two cautions: (1) can create hotspots on a few GPUs if traffic skews, (2) placement churn when hotset shifts could be costly.
Ellen V: agree. plan: soft affinity only 1% placement weight, plus decay window (15m) to avoid aggressive reshuffle. also tie to eviction priority so co-located shards get eviction protection.
Marco P: for warmup path, we can use affinity to pre-choose hosts for SOFT prefetch so reads go local rather than across NFS. reduces amplification.
ops-bot: telemetry note: model:redwood-4b last 14d shows 30% of requests touch >6 microshards across hosts; co-location estimated to cut cross-host reads by ~40%.
Zoe L: API suggestion: runtime hint `preferred_host_hint(shard_id)` returned by scheduler; router can prefer routing requests accordingly but fallback allowed. keeps routing non-binding.
Ellen V: rollout: start with a single cluster that has local SSDs. measure host hotspotting (GPU util variance). if variance < 12% and p99 latency improves, expand.
Marco P: also add a smoothing knob: when promoting affinity, rate-limit per-model promotions to X per minute to avoid spikes.
Zoe L: add a monitoring metric `affinity_promotion_rate` and an alert if it exceeds threshold.
Ellen V: action items: I'll add affinity section to warmup RFC with decay/window math and eviction interactions. Marco to propose promotion rate defaults. Zoe to add telemetry+alerts. Thanks.
